records.edition: On Divination,Loeb Classical Library,Cicero volumeXX,Harvard University Press,1923,William Armistead Falconer
records.speaker: Quintus
records.attribution: Reported soothsayer convention in rhetorical defense
records.source_account: Quintus reports postponement of an undertaking when a lung cleft occurs with otherwise sound vitals.
records.qualification: Falconer renders incisus as cleft; Latin literally concerns a cut/notched lung. No modern pathological identification; no advice to postpone.

records.edition: On Divination,Loeb Classical Library,Cicero volumeXX,Harvard University Press,1923,William Armistead Falconer
records.speaker: Marcus
records.source_account: Marcus reports practitioners treating an absent liver-head as strongly unpropitious.
records.qualification: Reported belief,not Marcus endorsement; ancient head label is not a verified modern anatomical mapping; present does not imply favorable.

records.edition: On Divination,Loeb Classical Library,Cicero volumeXX,Harvard University Press,1923,William Armistead Falconer
records.speaker: Quintus
records.attribution: Quintus reports Spurinna’s warning to Caesar
records.source_account: In Caesar’s throne/robe narrative,Quintus reports a missing heart and Spurinna’s warning concerning thought and life.
records.qualification: Falconer votive ox versus Latin bovis opimi (well-fed/fat ox); exact documentary translation label,not inferred ritual category or universal prognosis.

records.edition: On Divination,Loeb Classical Library,Cicero volumeXX,Harvard University Press,1923,William Armistead Falconer
records.speaker: Quintus
records.attribution: Quintus connects following-day liver-head account to preceding heart narrative
records.source_account: Quintus links next-day liver-head absence to the preceding heart account and construes both as forewarning Caesar’s death,not prevention.
records.qualification: Requires an explicitly linked earlier matching heart record in the ordered request; standalone absence cannot reconstruct chronology.

translation_notes.latin_witness: The Latin Library independently rendered digital text; underlying printed edition and manuscript genealogy unverified.
translation_notes.lung: pulmo incisus is rendered cleft by Falconer; no liver substitution.
translation_notes.head: caput iecoris and caput in iecore remain ancient source labels; no modern anatomical identification certified.
translation_notes.heart: cor is heart; bovis opimi is not independently evidence for a distinct votive category beyond Falconer wording.
translation_notes.sequence: Postero die explicitly marks following day; link and ordered-request convention are modern editorial safeguards,not an ancient input schema.
translation_notes.layers: All nine records are main dialogue/introduction. Translator/editor notes are not operative rules. Modern predicate design and status labels are editorial,not ancient algorithms.
translation_notes.speakers: Quintus defense and Marcus criticism are not a unified authorial endorsement.
